solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Uni mobs wrecked vehicle (7)

indicatorNotes.wrecked: something wrecked is smashed up, so its letters are broken apart and rebuilt

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: Rioting university students smash up a car.
annotation.walkthrough: Uni is British shorthand for university, so the surface pictures a student riot; the vehicle they wreck is the answer made of their own letters.
annotation.definitionFit: An omnibus is the old full name for a bus, a public passenger vehicle.

entries.clue: Annoyingly slow empty boat in river (6)

indicatorNotes.empty: an emptied word has its inside taken out, leaving only its first and last letters
indicatorNotes.in: the boat's remains go in the river

blocks.note: the Ouse, a river in Yorkshire and another in East Anglia
BOAT with its middle letters OA removed

annotation.surface: Someone grumbling about a sluggish, unladen boat on a river.
annotation.walkthrough: The Ouse is one of the commonest crossword rivers, and 'empty' is a standard instruction to keep only the outer letters of the next word.
annotation.definitionFit: Obtuse means slow to understand, the irritating kind of dimness that fails to see a point.

entries.clue: Exclusive new school in the East End (6)

indicatorNotes.in the East End: Cockneys of London's East End drop their H's, so HARROW is said 'ARROW

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
HARROW, the English public school, with the H dropped

annotation.surface: A smart new private school opening in the poorer East End of London.
annotation.walkthrough: Harrow is a famous English boarding school; the East End Cockney accent drops the initial H, which crosswords use to delete an H.
annotation.definitionFit: Narrow and exclusive both describe something restricted to a few, as in a narrow or exclusive circle.

entries.clue: School chief supporting check for dope (9)

indicatorNotes.supporting: in a down clue the piece that supports sits underneath, so HEAD goes below BLOCK

blocks.note: to check is to block or stop
the head teacher

annotation.surface: A headmistress backing a drugs test at her school.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Check for dope' reads as a drugs test, but dope is the person, not the drug. In a down clue 'supporting' puts the first-named piece underneath.
annotation.definitionFit: A dope is a stupid person, and so is a blockhead, someone with a head as dense as wood.

entries.clue: Go and shop as cheaply as possible (5,1,5)

blocks.note: a British euphemism for going to the lavatory
literally, part with the smallest coin there is

annotation.surface: Advice to hit the shops but spend as little as you can.
annotation.walkthrough: British public toilets once had coin locks costing one old penny, so 'spend a penny' became the polite phrase for going to the loo.
annotation.definitionFit: The idiom means to urinate, which is what 'go' means in the nursery sense.

entries.clue: One hour trapped in crash after motorway confusion (8)

indicatorNotes.trapped in: the hour is caught inside the crash
indicatorNotes.after: the rest comes after the motorway, so M leads

blocks.note: M for motorway, as in the M1
I is the Roman numeral one
a smash is a crash
H is the abbreviation for hour

annotation.surface: A pile-up on the motorway leaves someone stuck for an hour in the chaos.
annotation.walkthrough: H goes inside SMASH to make SHMASH, and M and I stand in front. The blog reads MI together as the M1 motorway, which gives the same letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A mishmash is a confused jumble of things.

entries.clue: Witty remark about a ditch full of water (4)

indicatorNotes.about: the witty remark goes around the A

blocks.note: a mot (bon mot) is a witty saying
A is used as itself

annotation.surface: A clever quip made about some waterlogged ditch.
annotation.walkthrough: MOT is borrowed from French bon mot, a witty remark, and it turns up often in crosswords.
annotation.definitionFit: A moat is a deep ditch filled with water, dug round a castle.

entries.clue: Quality of arrows left to kill seabirds aboard ship (11)

indicatorNotes.aboard: things aboard a ship are inside it, so the pieces go inside SS

blocks.note: SS, steamship
L is the abbreviation for left
to end a life is to kill
ernes are sea eagles

annotation.surface: An archery quality turned into a scene of shooting seabirds from a ship.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests arrows being used to kill seabirds, but the arrows belong to the definition and the killing is just END.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: an arrow's shaft is long and thin, so thinness is the quality the clue picks out.

entries.clue: A manic hello changed sad mood (11)

indicatorNotes.changed: the letters are changed into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: Someone's frantic greeting gives way to gloom.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a swing from mania to depression, which is the very condition the answer names.
annotation.definitionFit: Melancholia is deep, lasting sadness, an old name for depression.

entries.clue: Intermittent springs mostly come up around unfinished dig (9)

indicatorNotes.mostly: most of COME, losing its last letter
indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top
indicatorNotes.around: the reversed COM goes around DI

blocks.note: spas are mineral springs
COM(e) turned upside down
DIG with the G cut off

annotation.surface: Springs that bubble up now and then around an abandoned dig site.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a geyser, and 'springs' is really the resort word SPAS.
annotation.definitionFit: Spasmodic means happening in fits and starts, which is what intermittent means.

entries.clue: Cowboy gets all Uruguayan calves herded once at the front (6)

indicatorNotes.at the front: take the letter at the front of each word

blocks.clueFragment: gets all Uruguayan calves herded once
blocks.note: first letters of gets, all, Uruguayan, calves, herded, once

annotation.surface: A South American cowboy rounding up calves in the old days.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a picture of the answer at work: gauchos herded cattle on the Uruguayan and Argentine plains.
annotation.definitionFit: A gaucho is a cowboy of the South American pampas.

entries.clue: Girl assistant carrying hamper that’s short (8)

indicatorNotes.carrying: the assistant carries the hamper inside
indicatorNotes.short: DELAY cut short loses its last letter

blocks.note: an aide is an assistant
DELAY, to hamper, missing its Y

annotation.surface: A young helper lugging a picnic hamper that is too small.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hamper' looks like a picnic basket but is the verb, to hinder.
annotation.definitionFit: Adelaide is a girl's name, as well as a city.

entries.clue: What’s in Yangtze river plant raised for local animal (7,5,4)

indicatorNotes.raised: in a down clue, raised means written upwards, so REED reads DEER

blocks.note: the Yangtze is a Chinese river, so what it holds is Chinese water
REED, a waterside plant, turned upside down

annotation.surface: A riverside plant being grown to feed an animal that lives nearby.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Local' refers back to the Yangtze: the animal is local to China, so the definition only makes sense once the river is read as Chinese.
annotation.definitionFit: The Chinese water deer is a small tusked deer native to the reed beds of the Yangtze.

entries.clue: High on Everest, maybe when there’s less demand (3-4)

blocks.note: read cryptically: off (high, as meat going bad) plus peak (Everest, for example)
the fares and electricity rates at quiet times

annotation.surface: A climber high on Everest, perhaps in the quiet season.
annotation.walkthrough: The first half splits: meat that is high has gone off, and Everest is a peak, so OFF plus PEAK.
annotation.definitionFit: Off-peak describes times such as late evening when fewer people travel or use power, so demand is lower.

entries.clue: Pastry again taken before tea? Try something different (4,4,1,3,4)

indicatorNotes.taken before: the pieces are placed in order before the tea

blocks.note: a turnover is a folded pastry with a filling
anew = again
tea leaf, the dried leaf that tea is made from

annotation.surface: A second pastry eaten ahead of teatime, with a suggestion to vary the menu.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all afternoon tea, and 'tea' is not the meal but the plant's leaf.
annotation.definitionFit: To turn over a new leaf is to start behaving differently, begin afresh.

entries.clue: Deliverance when umpire accepts position (6)

indicatorNotes.accepts: the umpire takes the position inside him

blocks.note: ref, short for referee, an umpire
the lie of the land, how something is positioned

annotation.surface: The relief felt when an umpire agrees with a player's stance.
annotation.walkthrough: LIE as position is the golfer's sense, the way a ball lies.
annotation.definitionFit: Relief is deliverance, rescue from distress or danger.

entries.clue: Strangely inured accepting V&A is never changing (8)

indicatorNotes.Strangely: the letters are arranged in a strange new way
indicatorNotes.accepting: the fodder takes V and A into its letters

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 6 letters
the Victoria and Albert Museum in London
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: Someone oddly used to the V&A museum, which never alters its displays.
annotation.walkthrough: The V&A is the Victoria and Albert Museum of art and design in London; the ampersand is dropped and V and A join the anagram.
annotation.definitionFit: Unvaried means remaining the same throughout, never changing.

entries.clue: What encloses cattle a deer half avoided (8)

indicatorNotes.half avoided: half of DEER is avoided, so only DE is kept

blocks.note: livestock, farm animals
A is used as itself
DEER with its second half dropped

annotation.surface: A fence around a herd that a deer only half manages to dodge.
annotation.walkthrough: 'What encloses cattle' looks like the whole definition, but cattle is wordplay for STOCK and the definition stops at 'What encloses'.
annotation.definitionFit: A stockade is a fence of stakes built to enclose and protect a space.

entries.clue: God of old Babel (4)

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a babel is a noisy confusion of voices, a din

annotation.surface: A deity of the ancient city of Babel.
annotation.walkthrough: Babel looks like the biblical tower, which suggests a Middle Eastern god, but here it is just a noun for noise.
annotation.definitionFit: Odin is the chief god of Norse mythology, who gives his name to Wednesday.

entries.clue: Element of humanity and ecstasy includes God mostly (9)

indicatorNotes.includes: MAN and E take the god between them
indicatorNotes.mostly: most of GANESH, losing its last letter

blocks.note: man = humankind
E, slang for the drug ecstasy
GANESH, the elephant-headed Hindu god, without his H

annotation.surface: Humanity and ecstasy containing a trace of the divine.
annotation.walkthrough: The god sits between MAN and E. Ganesh (also Ganesha) is the Hindu god of beginnings, pictured with an elephant's head.
annotation.definitionFit: Manganese is a metallic chemical element, number 25.

entries.clue: Closure date of disused railway (8)

blocks.note: dead = no longer in use
a railway line

annotation.surface: The date an old railway was shut down.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a railway closure, and read literally a disused railway is a dead line.
annotation.definitionFit: A deadline is the date by which something must be finished and closed off.

entries.clue: Period of king holding power certainly forgotten (4,4)

indicatorNotes.holding: the king holds the other pieces inside him

blocks.note: King Lear, Shakespeare's king
P is the symbol for power
yea, an old word for yes or certainly

annotation.surface: A king's reign when his power was surely forgotten.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Forgotten' marks YEA as a word that has fallen out of use, the archaic form of yes; it says nothing more.
annotation.definitionFit: A leap year is a period of 366 days, with an extra day added in February.

entries.clue: Bit of help to net fish then hunt game (4-3-4)

indicatorNotes.Bit of: a bit of the word is its first letter

blocks.note: first letter of help
the ide, a freshwater fish
and = then, next
to seek is to hunt for

annotation.surface: A helper catching fish and then going off hunting game.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hunt game' reads as shooting wild animals, but game is the definition and hunt is SEEK. The IDE is a crossword regular among fish.
annotation.definitionFit: Hide-and-seek is the children's game in which one player hunts for the others.

entries.clue: Heavily-built rodent eating southeastern monkey (8)

indicatorNotes.eating: the rodent eats SE, taking it inside

blocks.note: the marmot, a large stout ground squirrel
SE, south-east

annotation.surface: A stocky rodent eating a monkey from the south-east.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Heavily-built' is there to pick out the marmot among rodents; it is part of the wordplay, not a description of the monkey.
annotation.definitionFit: A marmoset is a small South American monkey.

entries.clue: Spoil lie about report with alien which contains rubbish (10,6)

blocks.note: to waste is to spoil or squander
a paper is a written report
to bask is to lie about in the sun
ET, the film's extra-terrestrial

annotation.surface: Wrecking a report that lies about an alien, one full of nonsense.
annotation.walkthrough: The pieces are taken out of clue order, report before lie. 'Rubbish' sounds like a verdict on the report but is litter, and 'lie' is lounging, not lying.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the office bin exists to hold discarded paper and other litter.

entries.clue: Left cheated, taken in by a gang (9)

indicatorNotes.taken in by: the word for cheated is taken inside the gang

blocks.note: A is used as itself
a band is a group or gang
done = swindled, as in 'I've been done'

annotation.surface: A victim left swindled after being taken in by a gang.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Taken in' doubles in the surface as fooled, which fits the cheating, but here it is only the container signal. Done for cheated is informal British usage.
annotation.definitionFit: Abandoned means left behind, deserted.

entries.clue: Catholic city with the French court in charge (8)

blocks.note: EC, the postcode of the City of London
le is French for the
Ct is the abbreviation for court
i/c, in charge

annotation.surface: A Catholic city whose French court is in control.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Catholic' with a capital pretends to be the church; it is the lower-case sense, wide-ranging. EC is the City of London's postcode.
annotation.definitionFit: Catholic tastes are broad and varied, and eclectic means drawing on a wide range of sources.

entries.clue: Stray scent almost enveloping one (4)

indicatorNotes.enveloping: to envelop is to wrap round, so the shortened scent wraps round the one

blocks.note: WAFT, a drifting smell, without the T
I is the Roman numeral one

annotation.surface: A faint scent drifting round a lost creature.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stray' looks like a lost pet but is a homeless child here.
annotation.definitionFit: A waif is a stray, a homeless and neglected child or animal.

entries.clue: I finish cutting mullet? Horrendous (8)

indicatorNotes.cutting: I and END cut into the fish, going inside it

blocks.note: a mullet is a fish
I is used as itself
end = finish

annotation.surface: Someone finishes chopping a mullet and finds the result dreadful.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mullet' may suggest the haircut, which a cutting could be about; it is the fish.
annotation.definitionFit: Fiendish means devilishly cruel or dreadful, like a fiend.

entries.clue: Caught poem’s secret message (4)

blocks.note: c, caught, in cricket scoring
an ode is a poem; the 's is read as 'is'

annotation.surface: A poem that has been caught carrying a hidden message.
annotation.walkthrough: C for caught comes from cricket scorecards, where a batsman out caught is marked c.
annotation.definitionFit: A code is a system for sending secret messages, and by extension the message itself.

entries.clue: Mystic briefly shaped revolutionary branch of philosophy (11)

indicatorNotes.briefly: SHAPED is cut short, losing its D
indicatorNotes.revolutionary: the letters are turned over into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 6 letters
SHAPED with its last letter cut
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A mystic who briefly shaped a radical new school of thought.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' looks as if it trims 'Mystic', but trimming MYSTIC leaves the C short; it is SHAPED that loses a letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Metaphysics is the branch of philosophy dealing with being, reality and first principles.

entries.clue: Role needing quiet skill (4)

indicatorNotes.needing: the quiet letter needs the skill to follow it

blocks.note: p, piano, quiet in music
art = skill

annotation.surface: An acting role that calls for subtle skill.
annotation.walkthrough: P is the musical marking piano, meaning play quietly.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from the theatre: an actor is cast in a role, or given a part.

entries.clue: Choir ceased performing in area of York Minster? (11)

indicatorNotes.performing: the letters perform, putting on a new arrangement

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: The choir stopped singing somewhere inside York Minster.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Area of York Minster' suggests the nave or choir stalls, but it is the whole region the minster governs; the question mark flags that the minster stands for its archbishop.
annotation.definitionFit: York Minster is the seat of the Archbishop of York, and the area under an archbishop is an archdiocese.

entries.clue: What could make Clare go away (5,3)

blocks.note: the setter's reading: CLEAR, knocked off (anagrammed), makes CLARE
the straight definition

annotation.surface: Something that might persuade Clare to leave.
annotation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as an instruction, CLEAR with 'off' as an anagram signal, and its letters rearrange into CLARE.
annotation.definitionFit: Clear off is a brusque British way of telling someone to go away.

entries.clue: What overseer does is very mean (11)

blocks.note: super = very, extremely, as in super-rich
to mean to do something is to intend it

annotation.surface: A complaint that a supervisor's work is terribly stingy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Very mean' reads as miserly, but mean is the verb, to intend.
annotation.definitionFit: To superintend is to oversee, which is exactly what an overseer does.

entries.clue: Beginning to notice terribly serious mental condition (8)

indicatorNotes.Beginning to: the beginning of notice is its first letter
indicatorNotes.terribly: SERIOUS is terribly mangled into a new order

blocks.note: first letter of notice
SERIOUS rearranged

annotation.surface: Starting to spot a grave disorder of the mind.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Terribly serious' reads as a single phrase for very grave, but terribly is the anagram signal for SERIOUS.
annotation.definitionFit: A neurosis is a mental condition marked by anxiety or obsessive behaviour.

entries.clue: Deployed armadas line sea port (3,2,6)

indicatorNotes.Deployed: the letters are deployed, spread out into a new formation

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters
L is the abbreviation for line
anagram fodder, 3 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: Fleets are sent out to line up off a seaport.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sea port' reads as one phrase, but sea joins the anagram and port alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Dar es Salaam is the chief port and largest city of Tanzania.

entries.clue: Get over with a leap and bound sober (5-6)

blocks.note: a jumper clears a fence
bound for = headed for

annotation.surface: An athlete vaulting a barrier and springing away, stone-cold sober.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bound' sits beside 'leap' as another jump, but here it means heading for somewhere.
annotation.definitionFit: Clear-headed means thinking clearly, not muddled by drink.

entries.clue: Subdued glow has the ability to enchant surrounding loch (11)

indicatorNotes.surrounding: the word for enchant goes around the L

blocks.note: can = is able
to delight is to enchant
L is the abbreviation for loch, a Scottish lake

annotation.surface: A soft light with the power to charm the area around a Scottish lake.
annotation.walkthrough: L for loch (lake) is a map abbreviation used in Scottish place names.
annotation.definitionFit: Candlelight is the soft, low glow given off by candles.

entries.clue: Pragmatic statesman’s approach putting true pressure on drunk held by lout (11)

indicatorNotes.putting: the pieces are put together in order
indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, on means placed above what follows
indicatorNotes.held by: the word for drunk is held inside the lout

blocks.note: real = true
P is the symbol for pressure
oik, British slang for a lout
lit (up) = drunk

annotation.surface: A statesman's method of leaning on a drunken yob who is being restrained.
annotation.walkthrough: OIK is British slang for an uncouth, loutish person.
annotation.definitionFit: Realpolitik is politics driven by practical power interests rather than ideals.

entries.clue: Section of pretty pertinent class (4)

indicatorNotes.Section of: the answer is a section cut from the words that follow

blocks.note: the last two letters of pretty and the first two of pertinent

annotation.surface: Part of a class that is rather relevant.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pretty' reads as rather, qualifying pertinent, but it is only there for its letters; TYPE straddles the gap between the two words.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a class of things and a type of thing are the same grouping by shared features.

entries.clue: Work out shoe strength (4,4)

blocks.note: a pump is a light shoe, such as a plimsoll or court shoe
iron = strength, as in an iron will

annotation.surface: Choosing shoes that give strength for a gym session.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Work out' could be solve, but it is the gym sense; a pump is a British word for a plimsoll or flat shoe.
annotation.definitionFit: To pump iron is to lift weights, a kind of workout.

entries.clue: Feel aggrieved at being taken in by a media host (9)

blocks.note: per = a, each, as in 'ten pence a (per) go'
to resent is to feel aggrieved at

annotation.surface: Resentment at being fooled by a television host.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A' is the hardest piece: it means each, so it gives PER, and 'taken in' pretends to mean deceived.
annotation.definitionFit: A presenter hosts a radio or television programme.

entries.clue: Look again at compensation involving advert (9)

indicatorNotes.involving: compensation involves the advert, taking it inside

blocks.note: redress is compensation for a wrong
ad, short for advertisement

annotation.surface: Reconsidering a payout that involves an advertisement.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Look again at' means consider afresh, not physically look; readdress a problem is to tackle it again.
annotation.definitionFit: Address means deal with or consider, so the RE- prefix gives considering an issue a second time.

entries.clue: Following drug in drink come down in imaginary world (9)

indicatorNotes.Following: the word for come down is following, so it is written after the drink
indicatorNotes.in: the drug goes in the drink

blocks.note: a dram is a small drink of whisky
E, slang for the drug ecstasy
to land is to come down, as an aircraft does

annotation.surface: Coming down after a spiked drink into a fantasy world.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a drug trip, and 'come down' is the landing, not the after-effect.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the land of dreams is an unreal place that exists only in the mind, often said of someone out of touch.

entries.clue: Island not entirely in a former region of Africa (8)

indicatorNotes.not entirely: IN is not given entirely, losing its last letter

blocks.note: Rhodes, a Greek island
IN without its N
A is used as itself

annotation.surface: An island partly situated in an African area of the past.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a linking word placing the island, but it is fodder that loses its N.
annotation.definitionFit: Rhodesia was the colonial name of what are now Zambia and Zimbabwe.

entries.clue: One’s son on St David’s day is noble (11)

indicatorNotes.on: one's son comes on, placed after, St David's day

blocks.note: 1 March, the feast of St David, patron saint of Wales, written March I
one's, used as itself
S is the abbreviation for son

annotation.surface: A son born on St David's Day turning out to be an aristocrat.
annotation.walkthrough: St David's Day, the national day of Wales, is 1 March, and the 1 is written as the Roman I. The pieces come in reverse of clue order.
annotation.definitionFit: A marchioness is a noblewoman, the wife of a marquess or holding that rank herself.

entries.clue: Fur rug concealing broken rusk (7)

indicatorNotes.concealing: the rug hides the other letters inside it
indicatorNotes.broken: RUSK is broken into a new order

blocks.note: a mat is a small rug
RUSK rearranged

annotation.surface: A fur rug hiding crumbs of a broken biscuit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fur rug' reads as one item, but fur is the definition and rug alone gives MAT. A rusk is a hard dry biscuit given to teething babies.
annotation.definitionFit: Muskrat is the fur of the muskrat, a North American water rodent, sold as musquash.

entries.clue: Appointed politician to look after energy (4,4)

indicatorNotes.after: after means later in order, so the word for look is written after the word for energy

blocks.note: life = energy, liveliness
to peer is to look closely

annotation.surface: A politician appointed to take charge of energy policy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Look after' reads as take care of, but look is PEER and after only sets the order. A life peer is appointed to Britain's House of Lords for life, the title dying with them.
annotation.definitionFit: Life peers are appointed, not elected or born, to sit in the House of Lords.

entries.clue: Simpson possibly very good composer (6)

blocks.note: Bart Simpson of the cartoon, one possible Simpson
OK, fine, very good as a reply

annotation.surface: A Simpson who might be a fine composer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' warns that BART is one Simpson among several.
annotation.definitionFit: Béla Bartók was a Hungarian composer of the 20th century.

entries.clue: Earthy reds at first aren’t drunk (6)

annotation.definitionNote: Terran here is the adjective, of the Earth; in science fiction it is also a noun for an Earthling.

indicatorNotes.at first: take the first letter of reds
indicatorNotes.drunk: the letters stagger into a new order

blocks.note: first letter of reds
anagram fodder, 5 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: Earthy red wines are not drunk at first.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Earthy' and 'reds' suggest wine tasting, but earthy means of the Earth.
annotation.definitionFit: Terran means belonging to the planet Earth, a word common in science fiction.

entries.clue: Brook, perhaps main source of water (9)

blocks.note: to brook is to tolerate, to stand
a water main is one kind of pipe

annotation.surface: A brook as the chief water supply.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Brook' looks like a stream, the obvious source of water, but it is the verb, to tolerate.
annotation.definitionFit: A standpipe is a vertical pipe with a tap in the street, used for water when household supplies are cut off.

entries.clue: Become united according to law but without support (4)

indicatorNotes.without: without means lacking, so the letters for support are taken out of the legal word

blocks.note: legally = according to law
a leg supports a table; removed

annotation.surface: Two sides joining forces legally but with nobody backing them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Become united' sounds like marriage, which fits 'according to law', but it means form an alliance.
annotation.definitionFit: To ally is to join together, become united in an alliance.

entries.clue: Innocent child covered in gateau in US picnic party (8)

indicatorNotes.covered in: the lamb is covered in cake, sitting inside it

blocks.note: a gateau is a rich cake
a lamb is a meek, innocent person, often a child

annotation.surface: A little one smeared in cake at an American picnic.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a messy toddler; the child is a lamb, a standard figure of innocence.
annotation.definitionFit: A clambake is an American beach party where clams and other food are baked.

entries.clue: Just show blonde straight up (4)

blocks.note: the adjective: impartial, even-handed
the noun: an exhibition, as of farm produce or trade goods
light in colour, of hair or skin
honest, above board

annotation.surface: Just showing off a blonde who stands straight.
annotation.walkthrough: Four definitions in four words: just, show, blonde and straight up all mean FAIR, and 'straight up' is not a reversal signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Fair covers all four senses: impartial, a show or fete, light-haired, and honest.

entries.clue: Loose shark is swimming both sides of current (6)

indicatorNotes.swimming: the shark's letters swim into a new order
indicatorNotes.both sides of: the jumbled SHARK sits on both sides of I

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 5 letters
I is the symbol for electric current
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A shark has broken free and is swimming along either edge of an ocean current.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Loose' looks like the escaped shark but is the definition, meaning dissolute. The jumbled SHARK splits as RAK and SH around I.
annotation.definitionFit: Rakish means dashing and dissolute, like a rake, a loose-living man.

entries.clue: Chaotic system of odd alternative technology vehicle (7,9)

blocks.note: strange = odd
AT, alternative technology, such as wind or solar power
a tractor is a farm vehicle
